findings.finding: The sole rotation-derivative question uses R=I, so the two multiplication orders coincide and the derivative equals the skew matrix in that special case. The general source relationship is not meaningfully discriminated.
findings.requiredRepair: Add one question under the explicitly stated spatial convention that distinguishes Rdot=S(ω)R from RS(ω), and Rdot from the skew matrixRdotR^T. A noncommuting orientation/angular-axis example or a carefully scoped property question suffices; do not add another identity-case numeric variant.

independentCounterexample.point: The products differ and Rdot=S_times_R is not itself skew-symmetric; RdotR^T=S is skew.

sourceDisputes.finding: The determinant-based singularity test requires a square Jacobian; rank loss is the more general statement.
sourceDisputes.handling: Questions explicitly assume a square Jacobian where determinants/inverses are used.

sourceDisputes.finding: Negative-real-part eigenvalue criterion is a continuous-time LTI result; the slide does not state that scope.
sourceDisputes.handling: The stability question explicitly states finite-dimensional continuous-time LTI autonomous dynamics.

sourceDisputes.finding: Rotation derivative multiplication order depends on angular-velocity frame convention.
sourceDisputes.handling: Question explicitly adopts the slide left-multiplication/spatial convention.

sourceDisputes.finding: Displayed equality equates MAP argmax (selected parameter/model) with a posterior probability expression.
sourceDisputes.handling: Drafts distinguish model selection from probability and use the posterior product only to rank models; do not accept the displayed equality as a general identity.

sourceDisputes.finding: MLE is described as using only latest measurements, although the data-only versus prior-informed distinction is the substantive point. More data does not unconditionally guarantee accuracy/stability under misspecification.
sourceDisputes.handling: Questions use data-only versus prior-informed contrast and avoid a universal accuracy guarantee.

sourceDisputes.finding: Lower entropy alone is not a general measure of model correctness; an overconfident wrong model can have low entropy.
sourceDisputes.handling: Questions test uncertainty/class impurity and explicit entropy calculations, not an unconditional quality ranking.

sourceDisputes.finding: The slide defines a tree as connected directed and rooted, which is a particular convention rather than all tree terminology.
sourceDisputes.handling: Tree question is explicitly tied to the lecture rooted directed convention.

sourceDisputes.finding: BFS/DFS figures omit neighbor order and repeated-state/goal-test policies; several BFS shortest paths tie.
sourceDisputes.handling: Trace questions state complete adjacency, order, visited policy and termination; diagram-count question only counts the actual highlight.

sourceDisputes.finding: Heading says search trees but the body describes classification decision trees; general search trees are not necessarily attribute-test classifiers.
Claim that Euclidean A* always expands fewer nodes, reduces Big-O and ignores away-from-goal directions lacks hypotheses and is not a universal guarantee.
sourceDisputes.handling: Only heuristic-versus-uninformed distinction is drafted as reliable; the unjustified universal interpretation is excluded.

sourceDisputes.finding: Unqualified A* completeness/optimality and genetic-algorithm probabilistic-completeness statements need search-space, heuristic, sampling/mutation and other assumptions.
sourceDisputes.handling: Questions test definitions and explicitly attributed lack of a finite-step GA shortest-path guarantee; no theorem about all GAs is asserted.

sourceDisputes.finding: SVD, chain rule and Jacobian calculus are named in summary but not developed in the preceding L03 slides.
sourceDisputes.handling: Only category/role coverage here; detailed derivations require evidence from later lectures.
